title: One-pass approximation scheme for random-order streaming matching
formal: For each \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\), does there exist a one-pass random-order streaming algorithm returning a matching M with \(|M|\ge(1-\varepsilon)\nu(G)\) with probability at least 2/3, using at most \(C_\varepsilon n\log^c(n+2)\) bits of working space, for an absolute c and finite constants \(C_\varepsilon\)?
definitions:
G is any fixed simple undirected graph on a known labelled vertex set [n]. Its m distinct edges arrive once each in a uniformly random permutation, independently of the algorithm’s coins. The adversary may choose G but not condition the stream order on those coins. The algorithm knows n and rational epsilon, reads edges sequentially without rewinding, and outputs an actual edge set M after the final edge. A matching has no two edges sharing a vertex; nu(G) is the largest matching cardinality.

Space includes stored edge endpoints, counters, retained random bits, and the final output buffer. The output must be a valid matching on every run; the approximation may fail with probability at most 1/3, over both permutation and internal randomness. The same uniform algorithm accepts epsilon as a parameter, and C_epsilon is bounded by some computable function of 1/epsilon. The logarithmic exponent c is independent of epsilon. No polynomial dependence on 1/epsilon is demanded, and no processing-time target beyond termination is imposed. Thus the question is about space at each fixed positive accuracy, not an exact matching algorithm obtained by setting epsilon to 1/n at uniform near-linear cost.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proofs of the one-pass space, validity and approximation guarantees for every fixed accuracy, or prove that no such uniform scheme exists. A hardness result requiring epsilon to shrink with n must account for the permitted dependence of C_epsilon and does not automatically refute this statement.
context:
Assadi and Behnezhad improve the approximation factor achievable in one pass under random edge order. This shows that random order can support stronger guarantees than familiar adversarial-order barriers.

Their near-perfect-matching limitations must be read with their accuracy parameter. A statement at a shrinking accuracy does not alone exclude the fixed-accuracy scheme selected here.
why: The target asks how much random order can improve a severe streaming-memory constraint.

import_provenance.original_title: A one-pass approximation scheme for random-order streaming matching
import_provenance.original_statement: Can a single-pass algorithm find a (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching, for every fixed ε>0, using O_ε(n·polylog n) space when graph edges arrive in uniformly random order? Assadi and Behnezhad broke the 2/3 approximation barrier, but an approximation scheme remains a substantial open target.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This editorial target concerns random-order insertion-only streams, not adversarial-order or insertion/deletion streams.
